reports.verdict: CoreWeave beat on profit and raised its 2026 outlook, with its order backlog jumping to about $133B. Losses and debt costs keep growing.

takeaways.label: Profit well above plan
takeaways.text: Adjusted operating income was about $379M, far above the company's $200–260M target, on revenue of about $3.7B, up 168% from a year earlier.

takeaways.label: Higher full-year outlook
takeaways.text: 2026 revenue guidance rose to $13–13.3B from $12.4–13.2B, above analysts' roughly $12.9B. Management expects to exit the year at a $20–21B annualized revenue pace.

takeaways.label: Backlog jumped again
takeaways.text: Contracted backlog reached about $132.5B, up from about $104B at June 30, which suggests AI demand hasn't slowed.

takeaways.label: Losses and debt costs persist
takeaways.text: Net loss widened to $709M from $110M a year ago. Most of the remaining build-out is to be funded with more borrowing tied to customer contracts.

reports.verdict: Bitcoin's rebound produced a $409.7 million profit, but the media business still loses money and nearly $1 billion of notes may need repaying.

takeaways.label: Profit is bitcoin, not business
takeaways.text: Net income was $409.7 million, driven by non-cash gains: $378.1 million on digital assets after bitcoin rose about 42% in the quarter. Revenue was only about $3 million.

takeaways.label: Note repayment unresolved
takeaways.text: Holders of nearly $1 billion in convertible notes can demand repayment starting Nov. 30. Management cannot say how much will be repaid, plans cash and credit, and says no new equity is planned.

takeaways.label: TAE merger on schedule
takeaways.text: Shareholders vote Dec. 14 on the fusion-energy merger, with closing targeted by year-end. The share count would roughly double from about 300 million to about 600 million.

takeaways.label: Costs fell, media still loses
takeaways.text: Operating expenses fell 45% from the prior quarter to $26.5 million, mostly on lower legal fees. Adjusted EBITDA was still a $12.3 million loss on about $3 million revenue.

reports.verdict: Berkshire's operating profit fell 6% as GEICO weakened, but CEO Greg Abel more than doubled share buybacks to $9.6 billion.

takeaways.label: Buybacks accelerate
takeaways.text: Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its own stock in the quarter, up from $4.5 billion the prior quarter, and about $14.4 billion so far this year. Reports say roughly $2 billion more was bought in October.

takeaways.label: Car insurance weakens
takeaways.text: Insurance underwriting profit fell from $2.37 billion to $1.35 billion. Reports attribute this mainly to GEICO, whose pretax profit fell 45% on costlier accident claims and higher advertising spending.

takeaways.label: Rail and utilities grow
takeaways.text: BNSF earnings rose to $1.73 billion from $1.45 billion, Berkshire Hathaway Energy rose to $1.61 billion from $1.49 billion, and manufacturing and retail rose to $4.04 billion from $3.62 billion. That was not enough to offset weaker insurance and investment income.

takeaways.label: Cash pile still huge
takeaways.text: Reuters put cash at $356.9 billion at quarter-end. AP and Bloomberg cited $377.4 billion, which includes $20.5 billion of Treasury bills bought in September but paid for in October.

reports.verdict: EVgo cut its 2026 outlook a second time, but its majority owner LS Power has offered $2.00 a share to take it private.

takeaways.label: Second guidance cut
takeaways.text: 2026 revenue is now expected at $375-400M, down from $400-430M in August. The expected adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $15-30M. Management blamed slower EV sales and a weak summer.

takeaways.label: LS Power buyout offer
takeaways.text: LS Power, the majority owner, proposed buying the shares it doesn't own for $2.00 cash, about a 59% premium to the prior close. A special committee is reviewing it, with no decision yet.

takeaways.label: Charging growing, but less used
takeaways.text: Charging revenue rose 29% to $72M, but daily use per stall fell 4% to 283 kWh as automaker charging credits expired. Excluding those, use rose 7%.

takeaways.label: Spending pulled back
takeaways.text: Management plans about $100M less building spending in 2026, shifting some stalls into 2027. Net loss still widened to $49M, but available liquidity is about $787M.
